cc_gate.text: The Chase road is closed. It is being inspected. We have been inspecting it since Easter, and very thoroughly.
The Spirit Stone, they say. Down in the crypt at York, with Keeper Hester. Come back when you've seen a bit more of the country.

cc_archaeologist.text: Every field in this part of Dorset has something under it. We just dig a trench and wait for the farmer to stop shouting.
Pitt Rivers set the standard here. Draw it, number it, record where it was. We still do that. Mostly.

cc_keeper.text: Fallow deer all over the Chase. They've been here since the Normans, give or take. Muntjac too, tiny and shy. You hear them barking at night.
Walk quietly at dusk and you might get a sighting. Or a ticking-off from a roe, which is worse.

cc_walker.text: I'm walking the whole Ridgeway. Marlborough to Lyme Regis. Day six. Chalk, flint, chalk, flint. I'm becoming a hill.
The old ridgeways kept to the high ground to stay dry and out of the forest. They were drovers' roads. They knew things.

cc_ranger.text: Chalk grassland is one of the richest habitats we have. A square metre can hold forty kinds of plant. The sheep keep it that way.
Nightjars come in May. You can hear them at dusk, a long churring like a very small tractor.
